title: Retract a grounded two-speed landing leg to its travel stop and stow the crank
instruction: Raise the foot in low gear until it is clear of the ground. Push the same crank into high, wind the leg fully up to its travel stop, and stow the crank in its keeper. Withdraw both hands.
setup: Two YAM arms beside a rigidly mounted telescoping steel-like leg. A 230 by 210 mm sand shoe rests on a fixed pad, 305 mm below its retracted stop. The 355.6 mm folding crank starts deployed in low, its shaft shifts axially by 28 mm, and a fixed keeper receives the sleeve. The side bench leaves the crank orbit clear.
scoring: 0 for an early shift or unfinished retraction. 0.5 for lifting the grounded shoe at least 3 mm in low, then pushing into high and retracting into the final 5 mm of its 305 mm stroke. 1.0 for keeping the shoe there with the crank seated in its keeper and both hands withdrawn for three continuous seconds.
context: A driver raises the landing gear after coupling and secures the crank for travel.
reset_notes: Seed 0. Fixed gearbox, grounded shoe, selector out and deployed crank. Settle for 30 control frames.
fidelity: Full-size crank radius and A400 gear ratios. A single counterbalanced rigid carriage, simplified shoe, thrust friction and passive keeper approximate an unloaded shop fixture. The nominal 305 mm stroke ends at the travel stop. The model omits the second leg, cross shaft and trailer load. Simulated one-gripper operation and effort have not been validated on stock equipment.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 at 24,000/24,000 steps (1200.00 s, step_limit). YAM: 1.0 at 17,360 steps (868.00 s). Both scores verified from recorded trajectories.
